impl.summary: Skills W4 is built on top of W1 and W3. A scheduled task can now run a saved skill instead of a request. Each run is still a chat with the same ask-first card, $2 auto-run cap, last_thread_id and summaries. A fixed reply (skillCall) makes one run_skill call with the task's values and calls no LLM, and each file input is either a fixed file or the newest upload of that kind, read when the run starts. The Schedule dialog has a What to run choice: A request (as before) or A skill, which uses W1's form fields and shows the price before saving. The CLI has new commands: fuobe skills params, estimate, run (-p, --rows CSV, --engine, --yes, --wait, --out) and export. Migration 25 adds assist_schedules.skill_json and is listed in ASSET_REFS.
built: Already there from earlier packages, and reused as is: W1's estimate, run, verify, recipe and download?format=zip routes; run_skill and its insideSkill guard from W3; the model override in startSchedule; renameSkillRefs; and the assist_schedules entry in ASSET_REFS (it covered attachments_json only).

Storage: migration 25 (the next free entry; the brief's 'index 23 at 7d7a765' is out of date because main added 23 and 24) runs ALTER TABLE assist_schedules ADD COLUMN skill_json TEXT, which holds {name, values, sources}. skill_json was added to ASSET_REFS, and migration 25 is a new row in the migrations table of docs/ARCHITECTURE.md.

src/lib/assist-schedule.ts: the ScheduleSkill type, ScheduleView.skill, newestWords and skillTaskLine. skillTaskLine writes a skill task in one line, e.g. '/weekly-promo Product photo: your newest image upload · Product name: Lumen'.

src/server/assist/schedules.ts, when a skill task is saved: checkedSkill checks that the skill exists, runs by itself, is switched on, belongs to the task's project, runs on the task's engine, and that the values fit its inputs (a newest-upload input is checked with a stand-in). The saved prompt is that one-line summary, and a skill task stores no mode, connectors or attachments. A task is rechecked only when it is changed or resumed, so a task whose skill is gone can still be paused, renamed or deleted.

src/server/assist/schedules.ts, when a run starts: prepareSkillRun reads the owner's newest upload of each kind (never an account's), attaches the files and writes the first message. The chat runs on the offline planner, so approving the card later also calls no LLM. skillCall throws the reason when run_skill fails, so the task shows 'failed' with that reason.

src/server/assist/schedules.ts, when the skill is gone or off: a deleted skill, or one with no recipe, pauses the task with the reason (as a deleted project does). A switched-off skill, or no upload of the needed kind yet, fails that run with the reason and leaves the task on.

src/server/skills.ts: renameSkillRefs now also updates scheduled tasks. When a skill is renamed, its tasks follow the new name (skill_json and prompt). When it is deleted, its tasks pause with 'Paused: its skill was deleted'. The brief said a rename should also pause; I made tasks follow a rename instead, as projects and chats already do. Say if a rename should pause.
src/server/assist/schemas.ts: ScheduleBody takes skill (null switches the task back to a request), and prompt is no longer required at the schema level; checked() asks for it when there is no skill.

The Schedule dialog: a What to run choice (A request / A skill). The new src/components/assist/schedule-skill.tsx holds the skill picker (only skills that run by themselves and are on), W1's fields (RecipeField, now exported from run-skill-dialog.tsx), and for each file input 'Newest upload (when it runs)' or 'This file' with a MediaSlot. It also shows the engine or engine chip and a live price line. The Assistant and Connectors sections are hidden in skill mode, the approval wording fits a skill, and editing a skill task reopens it in skill mode.

CLI, bin/lib/skills.mjs: new helpers skillValues (-p parsing), csvCells (the same rules the server uses), headerInputs, toCsv (keeps each row's line number), exactCost, paramsTable, estimateLines, estimateProblems and priceWords.
CLI, bin/lib/commands.mjs, skills params: prints the inputs as a table with a sample run command.

CLI, bin/lib/commands.mjs, skills estimate and run: local files are priced with stand-ins and uploaded once, only when the run starts. A file named in a CSV cell is read from the CSV's folder, and -p fills cells the CSV leaves empty. A bad row is reported by its line number in the person's own file, and then nothing starts.

CLI, bin/lib/commands.mjs, the confirmation: run prices the whole batch, then asks 'Run 20 for $12.40? [y/N]' unless --yes or --json is given. Without a terminal to ask on, it stops and says to add --yes; free runs start without asking. A skill not yet checked on that engine gets the free plan check after the answer. --wait and --out reuse generate's wait and download code.
CLI, bin/lib/commands.mjs, skills export: saves W1's zip; --examples keeps the values the skill was made with, and --out can be a folder.
docs/cli.md: a 'Running a skill that runs by itself' section, the stale line saying the CLI can't run skills removed, and the new routes added to 'What it calls'.
tests/e2e/schedule-skill.mjs is new and is listed in DEMO_CHECKS in docs/handoff/verify.sh.
tests: tests/assist-schedules.test.ts has 7 new tests (26 pass). They cover: newest upload with no upload yet fails the run with the reason; save-time checks, with no prompt and no model needed (also through the routes); ask first gives one card with the recipe's price, the newest upload is read when the run starts (not when saved, and never an account's), and approving runs it on the mock provider; auto runs within the cap, and over the cap it waits with the reason; a fixed file keeps the task listed under assetUses, and a value that no longer fits fails the run with 'needs tagline (text)'; a rename follows and a delete pauses, the task can still be renamed but not resumed, and a skill removed behind deleteSkill's back pauses via Run now (422); migration 25 adds the column to an older database and an old task reads as a request.
Every skill task test passes a model that throws if it is called, which shows no LLM is called.
tests/cli.test.ts has 4 new tests (36 pass): -p parsing, CSV and TSV parsing with quotes, BOM and line breaks, header matching, toCsv line numbers, exact prices, and row lines.

tests/cli-run.test.ts has 6 new tests (21 pass): params; estimate with stand-ins and no upload; an unknown input or wrong --engine exits 2; run without --yes off a terminal exits 2 and does nothing; --yes runs estimate, verify, upload and run in that order, then waits and saves; --rows with -p filling empty cells, one upload, an ignored column noted, and --json; a bad row named by its line in the file, with nothing started; the terminal prompt 'Run 2 for $1.24? [y/N]' (no starts nothing, yes runs); export with --examples and into a folder.

Targeted runs passed: library.test.ts (the ASSET_REFS coverage test), dropped-branch-migrations, assist-skills, assist-skill-tools and public-signup (127 tests). tsc and eslint on the changed files were clean.

Full Vitest run (FUOBE_ACCOUNT_DISK_FREE_GB=1, --maxWorkers=2): 4984 passed, 7 failed, 3 skipped. Six failures are the known ones from main: comfy-reuse, dop-originals, preset-featured, soul-runs (2) and split-soundtrack. The seventh, worker-program 'a port another program holds', hit its 5 s timeout under load and passes when run alone (12/12); this branch doesn't touch bin/lib/worker.

Browser: tests/e2e/schedule-skill.mjs against pnpm dev in demo mode passed every check at 1440 and 390 px, light and dark, with no page or hydration errors and no sideways scroll. It checks the skill picker, newest upload as the default, the file slot, the demo price before saving, save, the list line, Run now producing a priced card with the newest upload attached, and Edit reopening the task in skill mode. I also checked by hand that request mode still saves at both widths, and looked at the screenshots. The dev server is stopped and .next is deleted.
left: The Skills page has no 'Schedule…' entry for a skill that runs by itself. The dialog accepts seed.skill, so adding one is a small UI change.
Scheduled skill runs were checked only on the mock provider. Real cloud or GPU runs need a key or a GPU, as everywhere else.
The price line in the dialog is an estimate per run. A newest-upload input is priced with a stand-in file, so a video-length price can differ once the real upload is read.
fuobe skills run --json starts without asking, as the brief says. Scripts that spend money should know this.
When the shared estimate shows a job that can't run because nothing is connected, the task's 'A plan waits for your approval (free)' still says free, because that summary existed before this package.
impl.docsNotes: docs/STATUS.md: (1) In Assist, scheduled tasks can run a saved skill ('What to run: A request | A skill'). There is no LLM in the loop, each file input is a fixed file or the newest upload of its kind (read when the run starts, always the owner's), and the same ask-first and cap rules apply. Deleting a skill pauses its tasks; renaming one keeps them running. Verified in demo mode and in tests; real runs need keys or a GPU. (2) CLI: fuobe skills params, estimate, run (-p, --rows CSV, --engine, --yes, --wait, --out) and export. docs/ARCHITECTURE.md already has migration 25; the docs pass may add one line under 'Round 5' saying ASSET_REFS gains assist_schedules.skill_json, and the round's migration count is now 26 (0–25). .agents/skills/fuobe/SKILL.md could mention 'fuobe skills run' as a way to run a saved skill.

findings.title: Migration 25 collides with the integration branch's new migration 25
findings.detail: After this branch's merge base (41819feb), claude/fuobe-parity-4 merged o/nm10-voice-design (8f2fa6f7, commit 49c8cfaa). That branch appended MIGRATIONS[25] = `ALTER TABLE characters ADD COLUMN voice_json TEXT;`. Both branches now have 26 entries, and both put their own column at index 25. `git merge-tree claude/fuobe-parity-4 o/w2s-w4` reports CONFLICT (content) in src/server/db.ts. When resolved, skill_json must go AFTER voice_json as index 26 and never at 25: a data folder that already ran the base has id 25 marked done, so skill_json would never be added, and every INSERT/UPDATE of assist_schedules would fail on the missing column. The branch's own test (`findIndex(skill_json) === MIGRATIONS.length - 1`) enforces that order once merged. docs/ARCHITECTURE.md says '| 25 | assist_schedules.skill_json …' and must become 26, with the docs pass adding 25 for characters.voice_json. The docsNotes count '26 (0–25)' becomes 27 (0–26). No other unmerged local o/* branch adds a migration.
findings.verified: Ran an eval of the MIGRATIONS array on each ref: o/w2s-w4 has 26 entries ending with skill_json; claude/fuobe-parity-4 and origin/claude/fuobe-parity-4 have 26 entries ending with voice_json; origin/main has 25. Confirmed the conflict with git merge-tree.
findings.fix: Merge claude/fuobe-parity-4 into o/w2s-w4. Keep base's voice_json at 25, append skill_json as 26 and renumber the ARCHITECTURE row. Rerun tests/assist-schedules.test.ts and tests/dropped-branch-migrations.test.ts.

findings.title: Optional or defaulted file inputs default to 'Newest upload', and a missing upload fails the run even when the input is optional
findings.detail: sourceOf() returns 'newest' for any file input with nothing picked, whatever p.required or p.default say. A new task therefore saves sources[id]='newest' for optional inputs too, and for inputs whose skill has its own default file. prepareSkillRun then returns {stop:'failed'} whenever no upload of that kind exists, without checking p.required. The results: (a) an optional input, or one with a default (e.g. a bundled logo), is filled with whatever the owner uploaded last; (b) with no such upload, every run fails with 'There's no image upload yet for “…”' for an input the skill doesn't need; (c) two inputs of the same kind both set to newest get the same file. W1's Run dialog leaves optional or defaulted media empty, so the server applies the default. The only workaround is to pick 'This file' and leave the slot empty, which is not obvious.
findings.verified: Traced the code: sourceOf line ~45, skillTask; prepareSkillRun's loop never reads p.required or p.default. The tests and the e2e check use only required inputs.
findings.fix: Default to newest only for required inputs with no default. Give optional inputs a 'None' or 'skill default' choice. On the server, leave a non-required newest input empty when nothing is uploaded instead of failing.

findings.title: The CLI confirmation price uses stand-in files; uploads happen after the answer, with no repricing
findings.detail: The brief says run uploads local files first, as generate --image does, with stand-ins only for estimate. skillsRun prices with fileStandIn URLs, asks 'Run N for $X? [y/N]', then uploads and runs with no new estimate. For a step that prices by input clip length (model.pricing.clipInput), a stand-in video is priced at clipSeconds 0, which bills the minimum: plan.ts:455-456 ('at the least they bill … until the server reads their length'). The real length is read when the run starts (generations.ts:1766). So the confirmed price can understate a video- or audio-input batch. --yes and the scheduled path are unaffected; the scheduled path prices the real newest upload.
findings.verified: Traced the stand-in flow and the clipInput pricing path. Not run against a real clip-priced model.
findings.fix: After uploading, estimate again with the real URLs. If the total rose, ask again, or stop without a terminal. Or upload first when a file input is video or audio.

findings.title: skills run --wait/--out exits 0, and --json drops the errors, when some rows didn't start
findings.detail: For a tool recipe with several rows, runRecipe returns runs[i].error for rows that couldn't start while the other rows still run (recipes.ts ~519-521). Without --wait, skillsRun returns EXIT.failed when started !== runs.length. With --wait or --out it returns finish(ctx, ids), whose exit code covers only the started ids, so the command exits 0. The per-row errors are printed as notes only when --json is off, and finish's JSON is just {items}, so a script loses which rows failed.
findings.verified: Traced finish(): `gens.every(succeeded)` covers started ids only, and the --json output has no run errors.
findings.fix: Return EXIT.failed when any run has an error, and include runs[].error in the --json output.

findings.title: Row errors from the run route aren't mapped back to the person's file lines
findings.detail: lineOf() is applied only to the stand-in estimate's problems. If /run refuses after upload, its RecipeError lines ('Row N: …') count lines in the CSV the CLI sent, not the person's file. This can happen when a real file fails a check the stand-in passed, such as a clip that is too long. The numbers differ when the file had blank lines or multi-line cells. Nothing starts in that case, which is correct.
findings.verified: Traced: the ApiError from the /run request carries the server's message unchanged.
findings.fix: Rewrite the 'Row N:' prefixes in a /run refusal with lineOf.

findings.title: 'Newest upload' can be a file Fuobe saved itself as an upload
findings.detail: Several server paths store files of their own with source 'upload': the Cinema palette swatch (cinema-generate.ts:54), brand logos including SVG (brand.ts:1014/1071/1394), Content Factory and faceless reference thumbnails, the demo voice wav (studio-tools.ts:360, faceless.ts:714), and Mix export wavs (mix-export.ts:109). A Cinema run with a palette, or a brand lookup, after the owner's product photo makes the swatch or logo the 'newest image upload'. This matches the Library's Uploads list and the literal brief, so treat it as a product note, not a regression. Owner-only scoping is correct: account_id IS NULL (storage.ts:221).
findings.verified: Found every saveFile/adoptFile call with source 'upload'.
findings.fix: Optional: skip machine-made names or kinds (palette-swatch, *-logo.svg, reference-thumbnail, fuobe-demo-voice), or say in the dialog that the newest file in Library → Uploads is the one used.

findings.title: A renamed skill's tasks follow the new name instead of pausing, as the brief asked
findings.detail: Judged acceptable and better than pausing. A rename keeps the same skill row and recipe, and renameSkillRefs already makes project and chat skill lists follow a rename. The brief's model, 'as a deleted project does', covers deletion; projects have ids, so a renamed project never stops its tasks. Pausing would silently stop a weekly task over a cosmetic change. Following is also safer when the old name is reused: a paused task left on the old name would later run a different skill once resumed. Edge cases checked: invalid skill_json is guarded with json_valid; the prompt's '/old' prefix is rewritten exactly; a recipe edited along with the rename fails the next run with the reason ('needs tagline (text)'), as any edit would. One residual: an approval card already pending in a run's chat still carries the old name, so approving it after the rename says 'That didn't start'. The implementer disclosed the deviation. It is not in docs/handoff/owner-decisions.json.
findings.verified: Read the code, and tests/assist-schedules.test.ts 'a renamed skill keeps its tasks; a deleted one pauses them' passes.
findings.fix: Keep it. Add it to the owner's open questions as a deviation from the brief, and say it in docs/STATUS.md as docsNotes proposes.

checks: Newest upload is owner-only: listAssets without accountId filters `account_id IS NULL` (storage.ts:221); the schedule routes refuse guests and accounts (isAssistChange → 403 assist-owner; tests/public-signup-visitors.test.ts:108); the test adds an account upload newer than the owner's and the owner's file is used. The sweep and the run route run outside runAsTenant, as owner work.

Newest upload with none: the run records failed with the reason, the task stays on and runs+1 (test passes). A deleted skill, or one with no recipe, pauses the task; a switched-off skill or one outside the project fails that run.

Newest upload is resolved when the run starts (prepareSkillRun), before the chat and price are made, so the card and cap price the real file; the test checks that an upload made after saving is the one used.

Cap and pricing: on the auto path the cap check prices planFor('run_skill') (estimateRecipe; an atomic pipeline sums every step) through withinCap. Over the cap or with an unknown price → approval card plus a 'Waiting for you: …' notice. On ask-first the card total equals estimateRecipe's total. All tested and passing.

No LLM: skillCall replaces the model for the first turn. The thread is created manual/offline, repick skips manual mode, and after approval the offline planner's tool_result branch (agent.ts:848-859) answers 'On it' with no second card. Every test passes a model that throws.

Save-time checks (checkedSkill): skill exists, has a recipe, is on, is allowed in the project, runs on the engine, and its inputs are known and fit (newest checked with a stand-in). Unchanged edits such as pause or rename skip the recheck; resuming rechecks.

CLI: -p duplicate or unknown input → exit 2. Off a terminal without --yes → exit 2 and nothing starts. --json skips the question (per the brief). Free and demo runs don't ask. Prompt is 'Run N for $X? [y/N]', and 'n' starts nothing. --rows parsing matches the server's csvCells/parseRows. lineOf maps estimate rows back to the file's lines (traced with blank lines and multi-line cells). Export passes examples=1, which the download route supports.

Targeted tests: 24 related files (assist-*, skill*, recipe*, cli*, dropped-branch-migrations, public-signup*, worker-program), 472/472 pass; tests/library.test.ts (ASSET_REFS coverage) passes. worker-program passes 12/12 here, consistent with the implementer's load-timeout explanation. The full suite was not rerun (implementer: 6 known main failures + that timeout).
tsc --noEmit: clean apart from Next's generated globals (LayoutProps/RouteContext/PageProps), which are missing only because .next was deleted (needs next typegen).
ASSET_REFS: assist_schedules covers attachments_json and skill_json; the test shows a fixed file listed under assetUses.
The e2e check schedule-skill is in DEMO_CHECKS and doesn't filter hydration errors (page errors and console errors fail it). The browser check was not rerun here.

UI keyboard: 'What to run' and the per-file 'Newest upload / This file' choices are role=radiogroup with radioKeys and radioTab; the skill picker is the shadcn Select. Request mode is unchanged apart from being hidden in skill mode.
Commit hygiene nit: d54c875b changes only a doc comment, and 448216e4 changes only a test, but both subjects read as visible changes. No [skip ci].
review.verdict: Changes needed before the PR, mostly at merge. The W4 build is sound and well tested: newest-upload resolution is owner-only and read when the run starts, the ask-first card and auto-run cap price the real recipe, no LLM is called, and the CLI's confirmation and row validation work as briefed. Must do: bring in claude/fuobe-parity-4 and renumber skill_json to migration 26, after base's characters.voice_json at 25, in db.ts and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md. Should fix: optional or defaulted file inputs defaulting to 'Newest upload' and failing runs when nothing is uploaded. Nice to fix: repricing after upload for clip-priced inputs, --wait exit code and --json errors on partial row failures, and row-line mapping for /run refusals. The decision to have renamed skills' tasks follow the rename is accepted; record it as a deviation for the owner.

applied: Migration order (finding 1, blocker): merged origin/claude/fuobe-parity-4 (8f2fa6f7, then cb1d3b3a once it moved). The base's MIGRATIONS[25] stays characters.voice_json. skill_json is appended after it as MIGRATIONS[26]. The docs/ARCHITECTURE.md row is renumbered to 26 (row 25 for voice_json is left for the docs pass). tests/assist-schedules.test.ts now pins MIGRATIONS[25] to voice_json and skill_json to 26.

Optional or defaulted file inputs (finding 2): the Schedule dialog starts only the first needed file input of each kind (required, with no default) on 'Newest upload'. Later needed inputs of the same kind start on 'This file', so two inputs don't read the same file. An optional input starts on 'None'. An input with its own default starts on 'The skill's own'. Both are new third choices, offered only for inputs the skill can do without. On the server, prepareSkillRun leaves a non-required or defaulted newest input empty when there's no upload of that kind (the server then applies the default), and the run goes ahead instead of failing. The run's first message says 'Logo: no image upload yet, so it's left out'. A required input with no upload still fails the run with the reason. Tests: a server test (optional newest input, no upload: a card, run_skill values without it, the task waits) and a test of the dialog's skillTask defaults (first needed input on newest, second needs a file, optional or defaulted inputs on none, a saved task reopens as saved).

CLI reprice (finding 3): when skills run would ask (no --yes, no --json) and local files were uploaded, it prices again with the real upload URLs. If that estimate can't run, it stops with the problems mapped to the file's lines. If the total rose (a free first price that now costs, an exact price that now varies, or a higher amount), it asks 'With your files it costs $1.50, not $0.62. Run 1 for $1.50? [y/N]'. Without a terminal it stops with exit 2 and says to add --yes. Tested: no starts nothing after the upload, yes runs, and an unchanged price asks only once.

CLI exit codes and --json (finding 4): with --wait or --out, a batch where some rows didn't start exits 1. finish() takes extra JSON fields, so --json includes runs[], each with its error and, for --rows, its line in the file. --json without --wait also exits 1 on a partial start (it used to exit 0). Notes say 'Row 4 didn't start: …' by file line, and 'Started … (1 didn't start)'. Tested.
Row lines in /run refusals (finding 5): a RecipeError from /run has each 'Row N: ' rewritten with lineOf, so it names the line in the person's file. Tested with a blank line before the refused row.

Newest upload wording (finding 6, the dialog option): the note under 'Newest upload' says each run takes the newest image, video or audio file in Library → Uploads at that moment, whatever put it there. It is plain text, not a link, so reading it doesn't leave the dialog. For an optional input it also says what happens when nothing is there yet.
docs/cli.md: the reprice-and-ask-again rule, the exit code for rows that didn't start, and runs[].error and line in --json.
rejected: Commit-subject nits (d54c875b changes only a doc comment, 448216e4 only a test): fixing them would mean rewriting commits that are already pushed, which the instructions rule out. Left as they are.

fix.finalSummary: Skills W4 is merged with the current integration branch (cb1d3b3a). skill_json is now migration 26, after the base's characters.voice_json at 25, in db.ts, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md and the test. Fixes: (1) In a scheduled skill task, only needed file inputs start on 'Newest upload'. Optional inputs start on 'None' and defaulted ones on 'The skill's own'. An optional newest input with nothing uploaded is left out and the run goes ahead; it does not fail. The dialog says the newest file in Library → Uploads is the one used. (2) fuobe skills run prices the uploaded files again and asks again (or stops without a terminal) when the total rose. With --wait/--out it exits 1 when some rows didn't start, and --json lists each run's error and file line. A /run refusal names rows by their lines in the person's file. Engines are unchanged by this stage. Scheduled skill runs work in demo mode on the mock provider on either engine, and that is what the tests check. Real cloud runs need a fal or Replicate key, and open-engine runs need a ComfyUI GPU (built, not verified with real providers). The CLI reprice matters most on cloud models priced by clip length. Public sign-up is unchanged: schedules stay owner-only (guests 401, accounts 403 assist-owner), and 'newest upload' reads only the owner's uploads (account_id IS NULL), never an account's. The CLI uses the same routes and rules as before.

The brief asked for a rename to pause them. Deleting a skill still pauses its tasks with the reason. Remaining edge: an approval card already waiting in a run's chat still carries the old name, so approving it after a rename says it didn't start. This isn't in docs/handoff/owner-decisions.json yet; add it to the owner's open questions.
